rounds.fact: LimeWire became one of the most popular peer-to-peer file-sharing programs after Napster's shutdown, before being forced offline itself by a 2010 court injunction.
Digg pioneered the user-voted news-aggregation format years before Reddit took over that space, and a single controversial 2010 redesign is often cited as the reason it lost most of its audience.
Blockbuster launched an online DVD-by-mail service in 2004 specifically to compete with Netflix, only a few years before streaming made the entire rental model obsolete.
Download.com (run by CNET) was one of the main places people got shareware and freeware software in the pre-app-store era, complete with user ratings and virus scanning.
Webshots was one of the most popular photo-sharing communities of the early 2000s, and was also widely used as a source for desktop wallpaper downloads.
